note: Verifies the post's claims about Vercel AI SDK 6 agent tool loops against the SDK's own runtime behavior, driven by a scripted MockLanguageModelV3 (0 model calls). For pinned ai@6.0.212 the verdict is deterministic: a step count, a content-part type, or an error class is what it is. Source of truth: probe-result.json.

api_surface_verified.claim: The v6 agent class has two names for one class, and maxSteps is gone from the surface.
symbols: ToolLoopAgent === Experimental_Agent -> true (same class, two names)
'maxSteps' in (ai exports) -> false (removed in v6; loop control is stopWhen only)

loop_control_verified.claim: The agent 'loop' is just re-calling the model; whether it loops at all is decided entirely by stopWhen.
observations: A) generateText + stopWhen: stepCountIs(5), scripted [tool-call, text] -> steps=2, tool executed once ({city:Seoul,tempC:21}), final text 'Seoul is 21C.'
B) same script, NO stopWhen -> steps=1, final text '' (empty), but the tool STILL executed (toolResults=[{city:Seoul,tempC:21}]). The result never returns to the model, so the answer is empty.
B2) stopWhen: hasToolCall('weather') -> steps=1 (stops right after that tool call)

tool_error_selfheal_verified.claim: By default the SDK catches tool failures, feeds them back as a tool-error part, and lets the model recover — the loop does not die.
observations: C) tool execute() throws 'TOOL_BOOM' -> generateText does NOT throw. steps=2, step0 content types = ['tool-call','tool-error'], final text 'recovered'.
C2) model calls a tool that isn't registered ('ghost') -> does NOT throw. step0 content types = ['tool-call','tool-error'], loop continues (steps=2).

structured_output_verified.claim: Types are a compile-time contract; validation is a runtime throw. They are different layers.
observations: D) generateObject with valid JSON -> r.object = {city,tempC}, runtime r.object.tempC*2 = 42

agent_class_verified.claim: ToolLoopAgent is a thin wrapper over the same loop, and its DEFAULT stopWhen is stepCountIs(20) — this default cap is what 'being an agent' actually means.
observations: F) new ToolLoopAgent({model,tools,stopWhen: stepCountIs(5)}).generate({prompt}) -> steps=2, text 'Busan 21C.'

F2) a never-ending model (always re-calls the same tool) with NO stopWhen: ToolLoopAgent -> steps=20 (default cap); the bare generateText -> steps=1 (no loop). Same model, opposite behavior. An endless model silently burns 20 model calls under the agent class.

migration_trap_verified.claim: v5 code that looped via maxSteps silently becomes a single step in v6.
observations: G) passing maxSteps:5 (rejected at the type level via @ts-expect-error) -> runtime steps=1, text '' (empty). maxSteps is ignored; the loop must be re-expressed with stopWhen.

not_measured.real_provider_behavior: The mock scripts doGenerate/doStream by hand. Real-LLM nondeterminism — malformed tool arguments, infinite tool-loop tendencies, provider-native structured output — is NOT reproduced. This run verifies the SDK's CONTRACT and control flow, not model behavior.
not_measured.provider_specific: Structured-output native support and streaming details vary by provider and are not visible through the mock.
not_measured.tool_error_override: The tool-error self-heal is the DEFAULT; onError / tool options can change it. Only the default path is exercised.
not_measured.usage_tokens: usage numbers are mock-filled placeholders, not real token counts.
not_measured.streaming_order: The fullStream part ordering (start -> text-* -> tool-input-* -> tool-call -> tool-result -> finish) was observed in the original firsthand run but is not asserted in this committed harness (it is order-of-emission, not a scalar); cited, not re-measured here.

cited_not_measured.claim: generateObject is marked @deprecated in the 6.0.212 .d.ts ('Use generateText with an output setting instead'); the recommended path is generateText({ output: Output.object({schema}) }), still experimental.
In v6 the agent system prompt parameter was renamed system -> instructions.
